positions.Q45: Article 13(2) requires a high-risk AI system to be accompanied by instructions for use, in an appropriate digital format or otherwise, containing concise, complete, correct and clear information that is relevant, accessible and comprehensible to deployers. Article 13(3) sets the minimum content at (a) to (f), several items required only where applicable, when appropriate or if any: (a) provider and, where applicable, authorised representative identity and contact details; (b) characteristics, capabilities and limitations of performance, namely intended purpose, expected accuracy including metrics, robustness and cybersecurity under Article 15 and known or foreseeable circumstances affecting it, foreseeable misuse risks, and, where applicable or when appropriate, output-explanation capability, performance for specific persons or groups, input-data specifications and information to interpret the output; (c) predetermined changes, if any; (d) Article 14 human oversight measures including technical measures to interpret outputs; (e) computational and hardware resources, expected lifetime and maintenance and care measures, including frequency and software updates; (f) where relevant, mechanisms to collect, store and interpret the Article 12 logs.
positions.Q96: Annex III lists high-risk AI systems under eight areas, by their official headings: biometrics; critical infrastructure; education and vocational training; employment, workers' management and access to self-employment; access to and enjoyment of essential private services and essential public services and benefits; law enforcement; migration, asylum and border control management; administration of justice and democratic processes. Healthcare decision making is not one of them. Healthcare appears within area 5 at point 5(a) (eligibility for essential public assistance benefits and services, including healthcare services, evaluated by or on behalf of public authorities, and granted, reduced, revoked or reclaimed) and at point 5(d) (emergency healthcare patient triage); health also appears at 5(c) (life and health insurance) and 7(b) (health risk on entry), neither of which concerns healthcare decisions.
positions.Q17: Yes, by delegated act under Article 7(1) read with Article 97, within the areas Annex III already lists and only where the risk of harm to health, safety or fundamental rights is equivalent to or greater than that of the systems already listed; both conditions are cumulative. Article 7(2) sets the assessment criteria and Article 7(3) allows removal. Before adopting the act the Commission consults experts designated by each Member State (Article 97(4)). The act enters into force only if neither the European Parliament nor the Council objects within three months of notification, extendable by three months, or earlier where both inform the Commission that they will not object (Article 97(6)). A new area cannot be added this way: Article 7(1)(a) confines a delegated act to AI systems intended to be used in any of the areas listed in Annex III, so a new area heading needs an amendment of the Regulation itself, and by 2 August 2028 and every four years thereafter the Commission evaluates and reports on the need for amendments extending existing area headings or adding new area headings in Annex III (Article 112(2)(a)).
positions.Q74: Marking AI-generated audio in a machine-readable format is the provider's duty under Article 50(2), unless the person developed the system or had it developed and put it into service for their own use under their own name, which makes them its provider (Article 3(3) and 3(11)). A person using the system other than in the course of a personal non-professional activity is a deployer (Article 3(4)); the Act does not apply to the obligations of a natural person using it in the course of a purely personal non-professional activity (Article 2(10)). Where the audio is a deep fake, meaning AI-generated or manipulated content that resembles existing persons, objects, places, entities or events and would falsely appear to a person to be authentic or truthful (Article 3(60)), the deployer must disclose that it has been artificially generated or manipulated (Article 50(4)); where it forms part of an evidently artistic, creative, satirical, fictional or analogous work that duty is limited to disclosing the existence of the generated content in an appropriate manner that does not hamper the display or enjoyment of the work. The information must be clear and distinguishable, given at the latest at the time of first exposure and accessible (Article 50(5)). These duties apply from 2 August 2026.
positions.Q95: Under Article 6(2) the systems referred to in Annex III are high-risk, and Annex III lists them under eight numbered area headings: biometrics; critical infrastructure; education and vocational training; employment, workers' management and access to self-employment; access to and enjoyment of essential private services and essential public services and benefits; law enforcement; migration, asylum and border control management; administration of justice and democratic processes. A use case is a specific intended use listed within an area: in seven areas as lettered points, and for critical infrastructure the heading itself states the use (AI systems intended as safety components in the management and operation of critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, or the supply of water, gas, heating or electricity). A system is high-risk only where it matches a listed use case.
positions.Q104: Annex X lists the Union legislative acts establishing large-scale IT systems in the area of freedom, security and justice, under seven headings: the Schengen Information System, the Visa Information System, Eurodac, the Entry/Exit System, the European Travel Information and Authorisation System, the European Criminal Records Information System on third-country nationals and stateless persons (ECRIS-TCN), and interoperability. It imposes no obligation itself; Article 111(1) uses it to identify the AI systems that receive a transitional rule. AI systems that are components of those systems and were placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2027 must be brought into compliance by 31 December 2030, without prejudice to Article 5, whose prohibitions have applied since 2 February 2025 under Article 113, third paragraph, point (a). The Regulation's requirements must also be taken into account in the evaluation of each of those IT systems under those legal acts, and where they are replaced or amended.
positions.Q6: The EU AI Act sets no formal minimal-risk category; minimal risk is shorthand for systems that are neither prohibited under Article 5, nor high-risk under Article 6 (a safety component of, or itself, a product covered by the Annex I legislation and required to undergo a third-party conformity assessment, or an Annex III use case), nor subject to Article 50, nor GPAI models. They carry no Chapter III obligations, but Article 4 AI literacy applies and Article 95 codes of conduct are available.
positions.Q10: A provider under Article 3(3) develops an AI system or has one developed and places it on the market or puts it into service under its own name or trademark; a deployer under Article 3(4) uses an AI system under its authority except in a personal non-professional activity. The roles are not alternatives: putting into service includes supply for own use (Article 3(11)), so a party that develops and puts a system into service for its own use is both provider and deployer, and Recital 83 requires cumulative fulfilment. Under Article 25(1) a distributor, importer, deployer or other third party becomes the provider where it puts its name or trademark on a high-risk system already placed on the market or put into service, without prejudice to contractual allocation; where it makes a substantial modification such that the system remains high-risk under Article 6; or where it changes the intended purpose of an AI system, including a GPAI system, not classified as high-risk so that it becomes high-risk.
positions.Q16: No as to the emotions: Article 5(1)(f) prohibits placing on the market, putting into service for this specific purpose and use of AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in the workplace, and the company commits the third act by using the system on its workers. The only exception is use intended to be put in place or placed on the market for medical or safety reasons; efficiency is neither. Stress is separate: Recital 18 excludes physical states such as pain or fatigue and names stress in neither list, so a system inferring stress as a physical state may fall outside Article 5(1)(f); on that branch a system monitoring and evaluating performance and behaviour of persons in work-related relationships is high-risk under Article 6(2) and Annex III, point 4(b), unless Article 6(3) applies, and the company must meet the Article 26 deployer obligations. Article 5(1)(f) applies since 2 February 2025; the Annex III obligations from 2 August 2026.
positions.CASE_D: Yes, where the surgical robot is itself required to undergo a third-party conformity assessment: under Article 6(1) an AI system intended as a safety component of a product is high-risk where the product is covered by the Annex I legislation and required to undergo a third-party conformity assessment, and Regulation (EU) 2017/745 is listed in Section A of Annex I at point 11. Under that Regulation the robot's class follows its intended purpose (Article 51(1)), which the question does not state, and a notified body takes part in the conformity assessment in classes IIa, IIb and III (Article 52(6), (4) and (3)), so the condition is met for a robot in any of those classes. Article 6(1) and the corresponding obligations apply from 2 August 2027.
